title: Gaussian density and tail asymptotic
statement: Let $\varphi$ be the standard Gaussian density, let $\Phi(t)$ be the standard Gaussian cumulative distribution function, and set $L(t)=2\log(1/\Phi(t))$, where $\log$ is the natural logarithm. As $t\to-\infty$, the ratio $\varphi(t)/(\Phi(t)\sqrt{L(t)})$ tends to $1$.
replaced:
Let $\varphi(x)=e^{-x^2/2}/\sqrt{2\pi}$, $\Phi(t)=\int_{-\infty}^{t}\varphi(x)\,dx$, and $L(t)=2\log(1/\Phi(t))$, with natural logarithm. Then
\[
\lim_{t\to-\infty}\frac{\varphi(t)}{\Phi(t)\sqrt{L(t)}}=1.
\]
